question: Does the response to repeated depth change when the identical complaint and 77 intents are presented as a native q1 request rather than the generic research request?
scope: Secondary analysis motivated by the completed training-partition research projection. It reuses the same examples, not a new independent benchmark.
source: Only the two inference projections in the previously pinned BANKING77 original-training bundle
sampling: Exactly the same 512 normalized complaint groups. No additional groups, official test rows, menu reduction, or new acquisition.
methods: Exactly the original six public-development worker method IDs, unchanged, at the same precision, slots and window
native_input: Empty state; exactly questions.q1; original instructions and ordered option_0 through option_76 criteria. Verify the two original byte-stream digests, all row identities, input hashes, and menu order.

endpoints.declared_choice: Use the actual typed native decoder output for choice accuracy, observed-class macro-F1, coverage and disagreements with the first highest-probability option
endpoints.full_precision: Separately score the unrounded ordered slot probabilities from the same forward for NLL, sum-over-class Brier, ECE15 and confident errors
endpoints.typed_probabilities: Keep native precision and its support visible; never fix a probability vector by rounding, flooring or renormalizing
endpoints.compute: Time the actual forward plus the typed decoder. No extra study state is evaluated for warmup.

contrasts: Match each method across research and native framing on identical row IDs and input hashes
Within each framing compare full naive two-pass with full one-pass and the split-only control; compare compact naive two-pass with the same physical one-pass payload
Report how the framing changes the repeat-minus-stock accuracy difference for full and compact separately
